newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong threatens to deport 92-year-old woman.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong threatens to deport 92-year-old woman.

text.p: After a major battle against illegal immigration by children, Hong Kong has now arrested a 92-year-old woman who faces deportation to China, a newspaper said on Monday.

The woman, Lam Ying, was detained in a hospital a week ago when her status became known and was taken in a wheelchair to a detention centre where she was being held pending repatriation, the South China Morning Post said.
Lam was born in 1905, six years before the fall of the Qing Dynasty. She came from the same village in China as a seven-year-old illegal immigrant girl who was repatriated from Hong Kong in April.
The old woman had been living with Hong Kong relatives for the past two years, apparantly to help her grandchildren, the paper said.

Immigration officers were not available to comment. They usually refuse to discuss individual cases. Illegal immigration, especially by children, has been on the rise in recent years spurred by the myth that illegals will be given amnesty after China takes back the British-ruled territory on July 1.

Between January and April 1997, 1,449 young illegal migrants surrendered to authorities against 540 for the whole of 1996. In the first four months of 1997, 7,406 illegal migrants, including adults, were arrested in Hong Kong around border areas, against 23,180 for the whole of 1996.
